label: Tenant Redis service connector
summary: Prepare an optional tenant Redis service profile with explicit credentials, memory policy and bounded observations.
core_boundary: Hosted application Redis is separate from the Core job transport and sessions. Logical database numbers or key prefixes alone are not accepted as a complete tenant-security boundary. This is a design-only connector proposal. Essential hosting, current actor and tenant authorization, native service drivers and recovery remain in the free Core. No production interface, publisher trust, installation or effectful capability is established by this metadata.
acceptance: Qualify the selected product/deployment and Core provider with dedicated instance or demonstrably sufficient ACL/command/key/channel isolation, authenticated transport and tenant ownership.
Bound memory, eviction, connection and observation costs; forbid broad database-wide flush/config/script operations or access to Core transport keys through a customer profile.

Exercise credential revocation, expired connections, memory pressure, unavailable replicas and restore evidence; refuse unsafe cross-tenant command scope and preserve Core background processing independently.

Declare observation-only, import or externally managed ownership before any integration request. Refuse competing writers for Core-owned resources; ownership handoff requires an authorized inventory, admission review and recovery plan.

Before implementation, qualify an explicitly selected provider/interface revision, supported compatibility matrix, immutable package provenance, dependency inventory and licensing model; no release is admitted by this proposal.

Enforce current Core actor, tenant and capability checks at each admitted request; keep credentials in scoped secret references, redact diagnostics and reject arbitrary destinations, shell commands or host/container sockets.

Demonstrate that disablement, removal, provider outage and commercial entitlement loss preserve essential Core access, hosted workloads, local audit and recovery; retain owned data unless a separately authorized purge is requested.
